fed_inflation.name: Federal Reserve — longer-run inflation goal of 2 percent

damodaran.name: Aswath Damodaran, historical returns on the S&P 500 including dividends, geometric average 1928–2022

wage_growth.name: FinPath teaching assumption: the 2% inflation goal plus 1 percentage point, near long-run labor-productivity growth (BLS productivity)

fica.name: Social Security and Medicare employee tax rates (6.2% + 1.45%)

income_tax.name: FinPath teaching simplification — a flat 10% stand-in, not a tax bracket and not your tax bill

budget.name: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau — the 50/30/20 budget (50% of take-home for needs)

direct_loan.name: Federal Student Aid — Direct Loan interest rates for loans first disbursed July 1, 2025–June 30, 2026 (undergraduate 6.39%)

standard_repay.name: Federal Student Aid — Standard Repayment Plan, 10 years for most Direct Loans

unsubsidized.name: Federal Student Aid — unsubsidized Direct Loans accrue interest while you are in school

g19_card.name: Federal Reserve G.19 — commercial bank interest rate, credit card plans, accounts assessed interest, August 2026 preliminary

cfpb_min.name: CFPB explains credit-card minimum payments. FinPath uses 2% of the balance or $25, whichever is more, as a stand-in. A real card can differ.

card_example.name: FinPath lesson example — a $3,000 balance in “How to Avoid the 5 Most Expensive Money Mistakes People Make in Their 20s.” An example, not a survey.

g19_car.name: Federal Reserve G.19 — finance-company new-car loans, Q2 2026 revised (amount financed, APR, maturity)

car_rule.name: FinPath teaching rule — a car payment above 10% of monthly take-home is flagged as tight. The unaffordable preset uses the greater of the G.19 payment and 20% of take-home.

bengen.name: William Bengen, “Determining Withdrawal Rates Using Historical Data,” Journal of Financial Planning, October 1994. The 4% idea is a teaching rule of thumb (about 25 times yearly spending), not a promise.

ssa.name: Social Security Administration — full retirement age is 67 for people born in 1960 or later. This model stops at 65 so the snapshots line up. That is a horizon, not a claim that you can retire then.

collegeboard.name: College Board, Trends in College Pricing and Student Aid 2025 — average published (sticker) prices for 2025-26

bls_oews.name: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, May 2024 national median annual wages

bea_rpp.name: BEA regional price parities, all items, 2023. U.S. average = 100. Wages stay at the national median, so a higher state price level means the same paycheck covers less.

school_earnings.name: FinPath teaching default — $0 earned while in school, so tuition and grants stay visible. Many students work. This is not a survey.

under18.name: FinPath teaching default — before 18, living costs are treated as covered by someone else, and the monthly investing amount is still invested.

monthly50.name: FinPath teaching example — $50 a month, the Decision Impact preset. The compound-interest lesson also walks through $200 a month.

raise_example.name: FinPath teaching example — a 10% raise, with half of the after-tax increase invested and half added to living costs. Not a forecast of your raise.

inflation.note: Used to show results in today’s dollars. One steady rate, not a forecast.

stock_nominal.note: Geometric average. A single steady rate hides crashes. Past averages are not a forecast.

wage_growth.note: Applied once a year after the first working year. Nominal, so it includes inflation.

fica_rate.note: Employee share only. Additional Medicare tax and the wage base are not modeled.

income_tax_rate.note: Added to the FICA rate as a flat effective income tax. Not your bracket.

needs_share.note: Needs take half of take-home, then the state price level scales that dollar amount. Money not invested is treated as spent.

loan_apr.note: Fixed undergraduate Direct Loan rate for the 2025-26 disbursement year.

loan_years.note: Standard plan length. Payments start the year school ends.

unsubsidized_in_school.note: Interest accrues while you are in school. A subsidized loan would cost less. This is the cautious case, not a recommendation to borrow.

card_apr.note: Accounts that were charged interest, not a teaser rate.

card_min_share.note: Stand-in minimum. Your contract can be different.

card_min_floor.note: Minimum monthly payment is the greater of this floor and the percent of the balance.

card_example_balance.note: Starting balance for the credit-card what-if. Only the minimum is paid.

car_amount.note: Average amount financed on a new-car loan at finance companies, Q2 2026 revised.

car_apr.note: Finance-company new-car loan rate, Q2 2026 revised.

car_months.note: Average maturity, Q2 2026 revised. The car is not counted as an asset.

car_tight_share.note: A payment above this share of take-home is described as tight.

car_force_share.note: The unaffordable-car preset payment is the greater of the G.19 payment and this share of take-home.

safe_multiple.note: Freedom progress = invested assets ÷ (25 × yearly living costs). A teaching rule of thumb, not a retirement guarantee.

retire_age.note: Model horizon. Not Social Security full retirement age.

school_start_age.note: School years in this model begin at 18.

tuition_2yr.note: Public two-year, in-district, published tuition and fees. Also used as a stand-in for a short trade program.

living_2yr.note: Public two-year average budget minus tuition and fees ($21,320 − $4,150): housing, food, books, and other.

tuition_instate.note: Public four-year, in-state, published tuition and fees.

tuition_outstate.note: Public four-year, out-of-state, published tuition and fees.

living_4yr.note: Public four-year in-state budget minus tuition ($30,990 − $11,950). Out-of-state uses the same living budget.

tuition_private.note: Private nonprofit four-year, published tuition and fees.

living_private.note: Private nonprofit four-year budget minus tuition ($65,470 − $45,000).

in_school_earnings.note: Set this path’s scholarship if you will not pay the sticker price. Grants are an input, not guessed.

under18_invest.note: Before 18 the monthly amount is invested even with no paycheck.

example_monthly.note: Default monthly investing amount and the $50 what-ifs.

raise_pct.note: One permanent raise on top of yearly wage growth.

raise_invest_share.note: Half of the after-tax raise is added to monthly investing. The other half is added to living costs.

trade.label: Trade or short program (2 years, public two-year prices as a stand-in)
